## Research question

What is the fair per-share value of Idorsia (SIX: IDIA) when its clinical pipeline is valued product by product using phase-weighted probabilities of success, and how does that fair value compare to the current market capitalisation?

## Summary

**Method**: Risk-adjusted NPV. Each pipeline product is projected as a revenue curve (ramp -> peak -> plateau -> patent cliff), converted into operating cash flows via a time-varying contribution margin (sales - COGS - Selling), discounted at a biotech WACC with a mid-year valuation date (30 Jun 2026), and probability-weighted using BIO/Informa/QLS 2011-2020 phase-to-phase transitions. Development costs follow the same probability chain: the current phase is certain, each future phase is weighted by the cumulative probability of reaching it. Parent-attributable equity value = Sum of product rNPVs + parent net cash - PV of unallocated central costs - PV of J&J residual royalty (cap CHF 272 M). Per-share value is divided by the diluted valuation basis (issued + J&J mandatory + warrants + unvested free shares) and floored at zero (limited liability).

**Scope**: QUVIVIQ (daridorexant, marketed), lucerastat (Phase 3, Fabry disease), and three Phase 2 candidates (CCR6, CXCR7, CXCR3 antagonists). The three assets transferred in 2025 to the ring-fenced Idorsia Investments SARL (aprocitentan, selatogrel, cenerimod) are excluded from the base case and treated as an option-like residual, see [Methodology](methodology.qmd) §*Structural note*.

**Main finding**: Base case fair value **CHF `{python} f"{BASE:.2f}"` / share** (equity value `{python} f"CHF {BRIDGE['equity_value_chf_m']:+,.0f} M"`) vs market **CHF `{python} f"{MARKET:.2f}"`** (IDIA.SW close `{python} MARKET_AS_OF`). The gap decomposes into **two upside catalysts** the base case excludes: (1) a residual claim on the ring-fenced SARL assets, and (2) a QUVIVIQ trajectory above the CHF `{python} f"{A.PRODUCTS['quviviq']['peak_sales_chf_m']:.0f}"` M base-case peak. The J&J convertible loan (CHF `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_PRINCIPAL_REMAINING_CHF_M:.0f}"` M remaining, matures 15 Jun 2027) is **not** an upside: the Pharmakon covenant forbids cash repayment of a convertible, so the principal settles in `{python} f"{A.SHARES_JJ_CONVERSION_M:.1f}"` M shares at CHF `{python} f"{A.JJ_CONVERTIBLE_STRIKE_CHF:.2f}"`, already in the valuation denominator.

**Reconciled fair-value range across scenarios: CHF `{python} f"{RANGE_LO:.2f}"` - `{python} f"{RANGE_HI:.2f}"` / share** (post-floor, CB 2034 if-converted applied where applicable). See the full note in [Results](results.qmd).
